messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: production-gateway: sudden spike in 5xx (0.3% -> 9.8%) over last 3m for route /v1/generate. Paging oncall: @alex :rotating_light:

alex: got the page, investigating. i'm on call. what's the immediate customer impact?

sara: grafana shows scheduler/batcher queue depth exploding and p95 timeouts on gateway. looks like HOL blocking on batcher shards in us-east1.

lee: confirmed logs show repeated `batcher.enqueue timeout` and `scheduler overflow` around 15:02-15:05. KV cache growth on some hosts.

mike: snippet from logs i grabbed: 
```
2026-03-15T15:03:10Z ERROR batcher enqueue timeout req_id=abc123 seq_len=4096 model=redwood-xx
2026-03-15T15:03:11Z WARN gateway 502 upstream timeout req_id=abc123
```

sara: metric snapshot: batch_queue_depth per-shard ~ [1000,1120,980,1050], token_ingest spiking, throughput stalled.

alex: @infra-bot please snapshot node status and top GPU/CPU for batcher pool right now. tagging ops.

infra-bot: snapshot: batcher-pool-us-east1-02 overloaded; GPU util 98%, CPU steal 25%, kv-cache resident size growth observed (24GB on hot shards). no pod restarts yet.

ops: recommendation: immediate partial reroute and enable emergency eviction for long sequence tasks. this should relieve HOL and lower 5xx.

alex: starting emergency reroute: creating routing rule to divert new requests with seq_len > 2048 to fallback-async variant. patch command queued.

sara: enabling kv cache eviction on affected batcher shards; set eviction_threshold=18GB, eviction_policy=LRU-ish.

lee: routing change applied to controllers; traffic shifted ~40% to fallback-async. monitoring.

mike: downstream 5xx dropping from 9.8% -> 4.2% in the last 90s. timeouts still elevated (p95 ~12s).

cs-jordan: CS: multiple customers reporting intermittent 502/timeout. notifying top 5 impacted customers and opening tickets. sending status update now.

alex: running heap + kv checks on the hottest node. command: 
```
kubectl exec -it batcher-02 -- pmap -x | sort -nrk3 | head -n 20
```

infra-bot: eviction executed on batcher-02; freed ~6.8GB kv-cache. queued items reduced by ~420 on that shard.

lee: HOL partially cleared across shards, p50 latency improving. one shard still has a pinned long request causing tail behavior.

sara: propose short-request prioritization to break HOL: throttle or deprioritize seq_len > 3000 so short requests flow.

alex: applied short-request prioritization rule: 
```
set-priority --target batcher --rule "seq_len>3000 -> priority=low, preemptible=true"
```

mike: metrics after priority change: tail timeouts dropped, 5xx now ~1.1%, p95 latency ~1.2s.

ops: keep routing rule and eviction enabled for 30m while monitoring. if any regression, we will roll back immediately.

cs-jordan: customer-facing note sent: "We mitigated an infra congestion causing elevated 5xx/timeouts. Routing and priority controls were applied; service returning to normal. We'll share a full post-incident timeline."

alex: logging follow-up items: 1) add permanent surge routing for long sequences, 2) cap kv-cache + tune eviction, 3) adjust autoscale thresholds for batcher-pool, 4) add perf tests for high-token workloads. assigning owners now.

sara: adding perf suite test for sequence-churn scenarios and a loadprofile that exercises long-seq bursts.

lee: i'll own runbook update for head-of-line (HOL) mitigation and schedule a tabletop.

ops: closing oncall page for now; alert status = resolved in monitoring but keep heightened watch for 1h.

oncall-bot: RESOLVED: production-gateway 5xx returned to baseline. continue to monitor for 60m. :white_check_mark:
